## What's new in SBK 10.5

SBK 10.5 advances benchmark lifecycle correctness, distributed orchestration,
local visualization, deployment portability, and release engineering while
preserving the latency-sensitive record and measurement hot paths.

### Correct benchmark completion and failure propagation

- File and other finite readers now terminate when a driver reports EOF.
  Benchmarks finish when all configured readers and writers have exited,
  instead of waiting for the original duration after no work remains.
- Writer-side `NO_SPACE`, `DISK_FULL`, and disk-error failures terminate the
  affected workers and propagate through benchmark completion.
- Lifecycle coordination stays outside the per-record writer, reader, PerL
  queue, and SBM aggregation paths. No new atomic, mutex, wait, or conditional
  work was added to those latency-critical paths.
- Distributed SBK/SBM failures now retain actionable host and component
  context, reach the final SBK-GEM outcome, and produce a non-zero process exit
  status without hanging metric draining or cleanup.
- SBM records the first authoritative failure per client while preserving
  later diagnostic context during distributed shutdown.

### Lower-risk latency logging

- PerL `DefaultLogger.recordLatency` and SBK `SystemLogger.recordLatency` are
  final no-op callbacks. The single Performance Recorder thread therefore
  cannot be delayed by accidental per-latency work in console logger
  subclasses.
- Loggers that require latency forwarding, notably `GrpcLogger`, retain the
  dedicated callback path required for distributed aggregation.
- Repository-wide agent guidance now explicitly protects SBK, PerL, SBM, and
  driver hot paths from new branches, atomics, locks, waits, and allocations
  without developer review and performance evidence.

### Independent, multi-run SBK Web Console

- The Local Web Console is now the independent `sbk-web-console` core module,
  reusable by SBK, SBM, SBK-GEM, SBK-YAL, and SBK-GEM-YAL without depending on
  the benchmark harness.
- One Web Console process can serve multiple simultaneous benchmarks on the
  same port. Every benchmark receives a UUID and independent board name,
  history, lease, and event stream, so File, MinIO, queue, and distributed runs
  can be viewed and switched independently.
- Default board names are derived from the application and driver when
  `-boardname` is omitted.
- WebLogger starts `SbkWebConsoleMain` when necessary and reuses an existing
  compatible console. Startup/reuse decisions, connected benchmark counts,
  browser counts, and shutdown reasons are logged for diagnosis.
- Console links include localhost, IPv4 loopback, hostname, and discovered
  private/public IPv4 addresses and are printed both at startup and benchmark
  completion.
- Idle lifecycle is browser-aware: the server remains available while a
  benchmark or browser is active and exits after the configurable idle grace
  period. The default is one minute.

WebLogger compatibility changes:

- `-webhost` and `-webstart` were removed; the console is automatically
  managed by the local WebLogger client.
- `-webminutes` was renamed to `-websnapshotminutes`.
- `-webtimeoutminutes` configures idle shutdown and defaults to `1`.

### Stronger SBK-GEM distributed controls

- New `-totalrecords` distributes one aggregate record target across all
  remote SBK clients. Fixed-count remainders are assigned deterministically so
  the exact requested total is preserved.
- New `-totalthroughput` distributes one aggregate MB/s target across the
  cluster with decimal-safe arithmetic and deterministic remainder handling.
- SBK-GEM-YAL supports the same aggregate controls.
- Invalid combinations with per-client `-records` or `-throughput`, timed
  aggregate-rate conflicts, insufficient totals, and mixed worker layouts are
  rejected with explicit diagnostics.
- Remote Java discovery and deployment now report the selected node-specific
  `SBK_JAVA_HOME`, preserve bounded SSH output, and provide clearer deployment
  and process-failure context.

### Self-bootstrapping JDK 25 runtime

- `gradlew` and `gradlew.bat` resolve Java in the order `SBK_JAVA_HOME`,
  `JAVA_HOME`, `PATH`, then the SBK-managed user cache.
- When no compatible JDK exists, the Gradle wrapper downloads the pinned JDK
  25 distribution, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, and installs it without
  administrative access. Subsequent runs reuse the cached installation.
- Unix locking and Windows mutex coordination prevent concurrent installers
  from racing. PowerShell execution-policy handling and bounded download
  behavior improve first-run reliability.
- Generated launchers for SBK, SBM, SBK Web Console, SBK-YAL, SBK-GEM, and
  SBK-GEM-YAL use the same resolver but never download during application
  startup.

### Centralized and validated configuration

- Runtime lifecycle, logger reporting, SBM gRPC transport, SBP diagnostic
  limits, SBK-GEM orchestration, Web Console timing/capacity, Java bootstrap,
  container, and build defaults now have module-owned properties files and
  validated configuration classes.
- Existing defaults are retained when environment variables or optional
  overrides are absent, preventing configuration externalization from
  breaking established deployments.
- Shared local HTTP link discovery eliminates duplicate hostname/IP logic
  between Prometheus and Web Console output.

### Automated release qualification and publication assets

- `./gradlew releasecheck` is the authoritative release gate for compilation,
  static analysis, unit tests, PerL concurrency stress, performance gates,
  installed distributions, black-box logger/launcher behavior, documentation,
  and publication metadata.
- The portable JVM functional harness covers System, SLF4J, CSV, Prometheus,
  Web, and gRPC logging; EOF completion; SBK-YAL; SBM; Web Console reuse; and
  SBK-GEM/SBK-GEM-YAL behavior without GNU `timeout` or OS-specific scripts.
- The `local-docker` profile automatically provisions two SSH-accessible SBK
  clients and validates real multi-client GEM and GEM-YAL orchestration.
- Release qualification and publication are separate workflows. Publication
  builds the current version's release contract without invoking or depending
  on `releasecheck`.
- Release assets include reproducible SBK, SBM, and Web Console distributions,
  agent documentation, per-core-module CycloneDX SBOMs, an immutable JSON
  manifest, and SHA-256 checksums.
- Multi-architecture `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` images are validated and
  published to Docker Hub and GHCR with SBOM/provenance attestations and Cosign
  signatures.
- Consumable PerL, SBK API, SBK Web Console, SBM, SBK-YAL, SBK-GEM, and
  SBK-GEM-YAL coordinates are published to GitHub Packages. Drivers remain
  bundled runtime plugins and are not published as independent libraries.
- Maven Central publication remains an independent, maintainer-controlled
  JReleaser operation using the same seven-module artifact allow-list.

### Build and portability improvements

- Replaced the legacy Creadur RAT Gradle plugin with Apache RAT 0.18 execution
  that preserves license enforcement while removing obsolete informational
  noise.
- Removed invalid dependency-path warnings caused by platform POM metadata and
  runtime-only JDBC drivers while preserving packaged runtime drivers.
- Release functional execution works consistently on Linux and macOS, and the
  Docker GEM fixture handles macOS SSH-agent sockets and port publication.

## Compatibility notes

- JDK 25 remains required; the wrappers can now provision it automatically.
- SBP remains at major version 4. SBK and SBM participating in one distributed
  benchmark must use compatible SBP versions.
- Update WebLogger scripts for the removed/renamed options described above.
- Custom subclasses can no longer override the final no-op latency callback in
  `DefaultLogger` or `SystemLogger`; use the explicit forwarding logger
  architecture when per-latency transport is required.
- `-totalrecords` and `-totalthroughput` are SBK-GEM aggregate controls;
  existing `-records` and `-throughput` retain their per-client meanings.

## Installation

1. Download `sbk-10.5.tar` or `sbk-10.5.zip` from this release.
2. Extract it, for example: `tar -xvf sbk-10.5.tar`.
3. Run `<extracted-directory>/bin/sbk -help`.

Standalone SBM and SBK Web Console archives are also attached. Container users
can pull `kmgowda/sbk:10.5` or `ghcr.io/kmgowda/sbk:10.5`.
